1.title: Optimizing Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Optimizing Applications. It covers the exam area Domain four: Troubleshooting and Optimization. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Apply concurrency concepts (four point three.one). Optimize memory and compute power (four point three.two). Optimize application messaging (four point three.three). Implement caching with A W S services (four point three.four). Detect performance bottlenecks (four point three.five). Use A W S A I tools to identify optimization opportunities (four point three.six). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain four: Troubleshooting and Optimization (twenty-two percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Concurrency
1.text: Concurrency. The figure shows this: Scaling and concurrency controls for Lambda, E C two and connections.

1.title: Concurrency, continued
1.text: Concurrency. Lambda reserved concurrency. Guarantees and caps concurrency for one function; protects downstream services. Lambda provisioned concurrency. Pre-initialized environments; removes cold starts. E C two Auto Scaling. Adds and removes instances with target tracking or schedules. Connection pooling. Reuse database connections; R D S Proxy pools for Lambda. Thread pools. Limit parallel work inside an application. Exam tip: Many Lambda invocations exhaust R D S connections equals R D S Proxy. Protect a fragile downstream system equals reserved concurrency as a cap.

1.title: Memory and compute
1.text: Memory and compute. Lambda. More memory equals more C P U; test several sizes: a larger size can finish faster and cost the same or less; use a power-tuning approach. E C two and containers. Match instance or task size to C P U- or memory-bound workloads. Code efficiency. Reuse S D K clients outside the handler; avoid repeated initialization.

1.title: Messaging optimization
1.text: Messaging optimization. S Q S batching (send and receive up to ten messages). Fewer requests, lower cost. S Q S long polling. Fewer empty receives. S N S fan-out to S Q S. Parallel, independent processing. S N S filter policies. Deliver only relevant messages. Lambda batch size and batching window. Process more per invocation.

1.title: Caching
1.text: Caching. Elasti Cache. Database reads (any data). D A X. Dynamo D B read latency to microseconds. Cloud Front. Origin load and latency for web and A P I content. A P I Gateway cache. Backend calls per stage.

1.title: Bottlenecks and AI tools
1.text: Bottlenecks and A I tools. Detect bottlenecks with Cloud Watch metrics (latency, errors, throttles, queue depth, C P U), X-Ray (slow downstream calls) and Lambda insights. Typical findings: a single hot partition, not enough concurrency, too small memory, too many small messages, no cache. A W S A I tools can spot performance bottlenecks, resource waste and code inefficiency; measure before and after every change. Exam tip: Measure first, change one thing, measure again. A scenario that shows a metric (high queue depth, throttles, high latency) points to the specific control above. Exam tip: R D S connection exhaustion from Lambda equals R D S Proxy; slow C P U-bound function equals more memory.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Hundreds of concurrent Lambda invocations exhaust an R D S database's connections. What helps most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: R D S Proxy. R D S Proxy pools and shares database connections.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A latency-sensitive Lambda function suffers cold starts. What should the team configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Provisioned concurrency. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A Lambda function is C P U-bound and slow. What is the simplest first change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Increase its memory. C P U scales with memory.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A function floods a fragile downstream A P I. How can the team cap it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Reserved concurrency. Reserved concurrency caps how many copies run.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An app sends thousands of single S Q S messages and costs are high. What reduces requests? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Batch send and receive. Batching reduces the number of A P I requests.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Repeated Dynamo D B reads of the same items need microsecond latency. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: D A X. D A X caches Dynamo D B reads in memory.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does provisioned concurrency remove? Answer: Cold starts. Question two. What does reserved concurrency do? Answer: Guarantees and caps a function's concurrency. Question three. What gives Lambda more C P U? Answer: More memory.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many messages can S Q S batch operations carry? Answer: Up to ten. Question five. What pools connections for Lambda and R D S? Answer: R D S Proxy. Question six. Name two caching services. Answer: For example Elasti Cache and D A X (also Cloud Front and A P I Gateway cache).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Concurrency: reserved (cap), provisioned (no cold starts), Auto Scaling, R D S Proxy. Tuning: memory drives C P U; test sizes; reuse clients. Messaging: batch (up to ten), long polling, fan-out, filter policies. Caching: Elasti Cache, D A X, Cloud Front, A P I Gateway. Method: measure, change one thing, measure again.
